newsitem.title: MEXICO: South American kids used in Mexico crime ring -report.
newsitem.headline: South American kids used in Mexico crime ring -report.

text.p: Colombian and Venezuelan boys as young as nine are being used in a highly organised crime ring that has robbed banks and held up Mexico City residents, a television report said late on Wednesday.
One Colombian boy, Omar Fabian Castro, 9, was arrested after being caught robbing a Mexico City bank of 37,000 pesos ($4,680) earlier this week, the Televisa network news programme 24 Hours reported.
He will be deported to Colombia, the report said.

Police also have captured a 10-year-old Colombian boy, Nicky Andres Cordoba, who particpated in the robbery on Tuesday of a Chinese man in which more than 119,000 pesos ($15,000) in cash was stolen, the report said.

After hearing news reports of the first case, a Mexico City woman called authorities to say she had given shelter to young Omar Fabian after he arrived at her home saying he had no money, 24 Hours said.
She led authorities to two Venezuelans, one 20 years old and the other 17, who had in their possession the money stolen from the Chinese man, the report said.
The report did not say whether police believe they have cracked the ring or if there are other adults involved.
